messages.author: ankita mehta
messages.body:

But it is giving me syntax error.
Can anyone guide me for the same.
This is the web link from where i got the parameters:
https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/ja0273851
#
I have attched these parameters as two files , one is pdf  and other is
leaprc.ff100 .
leaprc.ff100 is the file that i m sourcing in the amber.

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Fri, Mar 06, 2020, ankita mehta wrote:
>I am just using the modified force field parameters .
>But it is giving me syntax error.
>Can anyone guide me for the same.
Your "leaprc.ff100" is not a leaprc-like file that can be sourced from
the command line in tleap.  Instead, you need to use loadAmberParams to
load in a file like this.
The file format info at
http://ambermd.org/FileFormats.php#frcmod
indicates that these files are fixed format, with entries in particular
columns.  Your file is "free format", with just spaces between the
fields.  I'm not sure whether loadAmberParams will work on that or not.
Note that the supporting information file you used has the data
carefully laid out in particular columns.
....dac

messages.author: Kellon Belfon
messages.body:
1. I think the order you have is correct. The parameters in your modified
leaprc (leaprc.ff101) should overwrite any similar definition in the ff99SB
leaprc, if it is loaded after the ff99SB leaprc. To double check if you
have the right parameters you can use parmed.
parmed topology_file
writeFrcmod name.frcmod
Then you can look at the name.frcmod file to see if it have the parameters
you intend to use.
2. The warning is letting you know that you did not define enough
parameters for an Improper dihedral. Which leads me to ask this question.
Which section of the file, loaded by loadAmberParams do you have the
definition for HW OW HW? Is it under IMPROPER or ANGLE? It should be under
the ANGLE section.

messages.author: Carlos Simmerling
messages.body:
maybe you could tell us a little more about what you're trying to do. That
is a very old force field. Do you need that specific one, or do you want to
do similar work? You might take a look at this paper instead, it has the
same protein included but also many more, and is a modern force field and
solvent model that can be accessed in the standard Amber release.
https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ja5032776
--

Professor, Department of Chemistry
Associate Director, Laufer Center for Physical and Quantitative Biology
Room 119 Laufer Center, Stony Brook University, Stony Brook, NY 11794-5115

messages.author: Kellon Belfon
messages.body:
The file format is here: http://ambermd.org/FileFormats.php#frcmod
When you look at the frcmod, you will see the different categories of
parameters (Mass, Bond, Angle, dihedrals, etc). It will be easier if the
file you are loading into tleap with the loadAmberParams command is in that
format. Therefore, your angles should be under the section ANGLE, your
dihedrals should be under your section DIHEDRAL, etc.  This should fix the
warning you are getting. For example, HW OW HW   100   104.52 should be
under the ANGLE section.
You can look at your frcmod parameters and compare them to the parameters
in the loadAmberParams file.

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Tue, Mar 10, 2020, ankita mehta wrote:
>
>3. I am getting some warning when I load modified FF as follows:
>
>Improper torsion lines
>I want  to correct this warning...
This is a tough issue.  There are expected "missing" improper torsions
for systems with fused rings (like purines and tryptophan).  This arose
about 35 years ago when someone (and it wasnt' me...) decided that a few
milliseconds (back then, a few microseonds now) could be saved by by
leaving these out of the force field, rather than having them in there
with zero force constants.
The obvious problem is that real warnings about missing impropers can
get lost in the midst of these innocuous ones.  I'm hoping that *some*
Amber user would like to get a gold star by adding in the zero-force
constant impropers that are needed to remove the warnings for standard
proteins and nucleic acids....
Most likely, however: you can just ignore these warnings for now.
That's what everyone else does....
....dac
